clues: This town sits on the east coast of a big island in west Canada. It looks out on the Strait of Georgia, a wide arm of the sea.
Summers here are warm and dry, and winters are mild. Rich soil and rich seas drew the first folk here long ago for food.
This place was cut off from the world for more than fifty years, reached just by ship. Roads and a rail line came in the First World War.
From most streets you can see a huge glacier close by. It is the one sight folk link most with this town.
This town is home to a Royal Canadian Air Force base. Planes for war and trade both use its runways each day.
